title: Feedback from GP practices and community pharmacies on medicines
respondents: GP practice staff (GPs and other prescribers, practice and primary care network pharmacists, prescription clerks, practice managers) and community pharmacy staff (pharmacists, technicians, dispensers) who worked with us on medicines in the last 12 months
summary: A short yearly survey for GP practices and community pharmacies: how well we communicate, follow advice, share information and work in partnership, and how we handle medicines support with you: telling you when support starts or changes, problems, repeat orders, review requests, supply problems, collections, hospital discharges and our requests. About 7 minutes.
purpose: Medicines support is the shared work where a failure between us, the GP practice and the pharmacy most often harms someone: a change not passed on, a repeat ordered too late, a discrepancy left unresolved. This survey gives the partner view of whether we keep our side of the arrangements in the Medicines Management Policy and the Ordering, Collecting, Storing and Disposing of Medicines Procedure. It replaces the professionals' survey (SUR-PRO-001) for these recipients, so it asks the same four themes (communicate, follow advice, share information, work in partnership) and the shared overall rating, which join the yearly professionals' result. The Registered Manager, our medicines lead, reads the results for the quarterly medicines governance report.

timing.when: Once a year, on the first working day of February with the professionals' survey, open 4 weeks; sent instead of SUR-PRO-001 to GP practices and community pharmacies

qualityStatements: How staff, teams and services work together

introduction:
{{organisation}} would like your view of how we work with you on the medicines of people we both support. It takes about 7 minutes and works on a phone. Taking part is up to you. Please do not name anyone we support. If you write the reference number from our email, we know which practice or pharmacy answered and can follow up; if you leave it blank, we will still act on what you tell us.

This survey is not for urgent concerns. If you are worried about someone's medicines or safety now, phone our office (out of hours, our on-call number). In an emergency, call 999.
privacyNotice:
{{organisation}} uses your answers to make medicines support safer and to improve how we work with practices and pharmacies. Our legal reason is our legitimate interest in running a good, safe service.

This survey is not anonymous. We ask where you work, and if you write the reference number or give your details, your answers are linked to your organisation or to you so we can follow them up. In a small area, a setting and an organisation may identify you. Only our Registered Manager and Deputy Manager look at individual answers. Reports show combined results only, for groups of 5 or more. If you tell us someone may be at risk of harm, we will tell our safeguarding lead and may tell the council.

We keep your answers for 3 years after the survey closes, under our Records Management and Retention Policy. You can ask to see, correct or delete your information, or object to our using it, by contacting our office or our Data Protection Officer (details on our website). You can also complain to the Information Commission.

howToRun: The Deputy Manager runs it under the Compliments, Feedback and Involvement Procedure, alongside the professionals' survey. CareFlow cannot yet send a survey to named people outside the organisation, so this is a public form: each year publish a new copy of this template on the first working day of February with an end date 4 weeks later.

In January, build the list from the GP practice and supplying pharmacy recorded for everyone who had medicines support in the last 12 months, and take these practices and pharmacies off the professionals' survey list (SUR-PRO-001): never both in a year. Send one email per organisation, with a reference number, to the practice manager or prescription team inbox and the pharmacy's shared NHS mailbox, asking them to forward it to the prescribers, practice pharmacists and pharmacists who deal with us; several answers from one organisation are welcome. Keep the list of reference numbers with the invitations, because a public form cannot tell us who answered. Do not send the discharge teams' survey (SUR-PRO-003) to a practice pharmacist within 4 weeks.

CareFlow cannot send reminders for a public form: email one reminder after 2 weeks to organisations that have not given their reference number in an answer. Where you work is required; name and organisation are asked only from those who want to be contacted.

Who may open individual answers: the Deputy Manager and the Registered Manager. This is set in Who can see the answers: individual responses are limited to the Deputy Manager and the Registered Manager, and results to the Deputy Manager, the Registered Manager and the medicines lead, showing from 5 answers. Super Admin, Admin and the person who made the survey can always see both, so keep those roles to staff who may open them.
actingOnResults: Read each response the working day it arrives and act under the alerts below. Phone back only through the organisation's main number, found independently, and raise any issue about one person by phone or secure email, never through the survey (Confidentiality and Information Sharing Policy). With no reference number or contact details, act on the information given and record it; never try to identify who answered.

How to count: positive means Very good or Good, or Always or Usually, leaving out Don't know and Does not apply to me, with numbers shown. Report GP practice and pharmacy results separately only where each has 5 or more; otherwise combine them as medicines partners. The four shared items and the overall rating are also pooled with the other professionals' surveys (SUR-PRO-001, 002 and 005) as the yearly professionals' result. Compare year on year, and alongside medicines incidents and overdue medicines reviews.

The Deputy Manager writes the report within 6 weeks of closing, with actions in the service improvement plan within 5 working days. It goes into the next quarterly medicines governance report and to the Directors within 3 months (Governance and Quality Assurance Policy). Results and actions go to everyone asked within 3 months of closing, and the May You said, we did summary goes to everyone on the list. Keep answers for 3 years after the survey closes, under the Records Management and Retention Policy.

alerts.when: A comment describing possible abuse, neglect or a person at risk, including medicines withheld, misused or diverted.
alerts.action: Tell the safeguarding lead the same working day; the lead decides within 1 hour and refers the same working day where needed (Safeguarding Concerns: Reporting, Referral and Enquiry Procedure). Phone back through the organisation's main number where it is known.

alerts.when: A comment describing a medicines error, near miss, missed time-sensitive dose or dispensing problem.
alerts.action: Record it in the incident log the same working day and get clinical advice at once if a person may still be affected (Medication Errors, Near Misses and Incidents Procedure); raise a dispensing error with the pharmacy the same day (Ordering, Collecting, Storing and Disposing of Medicines Procedure).

alerts.when: A comment expressing dissatisfaction that needs a response.
alerts.action: Record it as a complaint the same day and acknowledge it within 3 working days where the professional can be contacted (Complaints Policy and Procedure).

alerts.when: "Do we tell you when we start, change or stop helping someone with their medicines?" answered Rarely or Never.
alerts.action: The Registered Manager (as medicines lead, or the Deputy Manager on their behalf) has the last 3 months' notifications to that practice or pharmacy checked within 5 working days, where it can be identified, and any missing ones sent (Medicines Management Policy); otherwise a sample across practices and pharmacies is checked. An action goes into the service improvement plan within 5 working days.

rule.task: Medicines support changes not notified: check

alerts.when: Repeat requests not reaching the practice in good time: Rarely or Never.
alerts.action: The Deputy Manager checks order and receipt records against run-out dates within 5 working days, agrees the ordering route with the practice where it can be identified, and asks to align repeats onto one cycle (Ordering, Collecting, Storing and Disposing of Medicines Procedure). Care Coordinators place the orders, so they are told only what to change, never the answer.

rule.task: Late repeat requests: check orders against run-out dates

alerts.when: Supply problems not told promptly, or collections and deliveries not working: Rarely or Never.
alerts.action: The Deputy Manager agrees supply, collection and delivery arrangements with the pharmacy within 5 working days, where it can be identified, and tells the Care Coordinators only what to change, never the answer (Ordering, Collecting, Storing and Disposing of Medicines Procedure).

rule.task: Pharmacy supply or collection problems: agree arrangements

alerts.when: Communicate, follow advice, share information, partnership or overall answered Poor or Very poor; or medicines problems, review requests, hospital discharge differences or appropriate requests answered Rarely or Never.
alerts.action: The Registered Manager contacts the practice or pharmacy lead within 5 working days through its main number, where it can be identified, and adds an action to the service improvement plan within 5 working days (Compliments, Feedback and Involvement Procedure).

rule.task: Medicines partner concern: contact and add action

alerts.when: A compliment about a team or care worker.
alerts.action: Record it the same working day and pass it on within 5 working days (Compliments, Feedback and Involvement Procedure).

alerts.when: "Would you like someone to contact you about your answers?" answered Yes.
alerts.action: The Deputy Manager or Registered Manager contacts them within 5 working days, through their organisation's main number.

rule.task: Medicines partner asked to be contacted
